one_liner: Small V8-based JavaScript runtime with C++ bindings; scores 1.09-1.41x Node 26 on the v8-v7 suite.
what_it_does: lo is a minimal JavaScript runtime: a C++ embedder around a prebuilt V8 static library (just-js/v8 releases) plus native bindings for system calls, epoll/kqueue, libcurl, zlib inflate and OpenSSL, packaged as one executable that runs a script with 'lo file.js'. It does not implement the Node.js API; a Node compatibility layer is only proposed (open issues #57-#59, October 2026), so Node programs and npm packages need porting.
how_it_is_fast: For pure-JavaScript compute it is V8's own JIT, so the edge over Node comes from embedding a newer V8 (lo 0.0.33-pre ships V8 15.2; Node 26.10.0 bundles V8 14.6.202.34) with its own isolate setup and flags ('--use-strict --turbo-fast-api-calls --cppgc-young-generation', 2 platform threads) and no Node bootstrap layer. Native bindings are registered as V8 Fast API calls (v8::CFunction), which TurboFan can call directly instead of through the slow FunctionCallbackInfo path; this matters for I/O-heavy code, not for the v8-v7 suite.
when_to_use: Self-contained scripts or services you control end to end and can write against lo's own bindings, where you want a single small binary (57 MB vs Node's 111 MB on the ubuntu runner in the benchmark table).
CPU-bound JavaScript on macOS arm64, where the measured gap to Node 26 is largest (52785 vs 37405 score, about 1.26x even with the Splay test excluded, derived from page data).
Experiments with V8 Fast API bindings to C libraries, or with tracking new V8 releases quickly (releases moved V8 from 14.4 to 15.2 within August 2026).
Startup- or footprint-sensitive tooling where Node's bootstrap cost is the problem and Node API compatibility is not needed.
when_not_to_use: Any code that depends on Node.js APIs or npm packages: there is no compatibility layer yet.

When you only need raw V8 speed: plain d8 15.7 outscored lo on every platform in the same table (ubuntu 48107, macOS arm64 64220, windows 46932), and on windows lo trails Node on Richards and DeltaBlue.
Production or long-term-support needs: versions are 0.0.x pre-releases, Intl is reported broken (issue #31), and macOS arm64 and Linux arm64 build problems are open (#49, #27).
Windows deployments that need parity with Linux: the windows margin over Node is about 1.01x once Splay is excluded (derived from page data), and build quirks are open (#55).

integration.form: standalone runtime executable (built with make, or prebuilt release binaries)
integration.dependencies: prebuilt libv8_monolith from just-js/v8 releases, libcurl, OpenSSL (libssl), zlib; Visual Studio build tools and make on Windows
integration.min_toolchain: clang/clang++ with C++20 (Makefile default CC=clang, -std=c++20); MSVC cl /std:c++20 on Windows
integration.platforms: Linux x64 and arm64, macOS arm64 and x64, Windows x64

gotchas: Default V8 flags in main.h include --use-strict, so every script runs in strict mode; sloppy-mode code (implicit globals, with statements) fails rather than running as it would under Node.
The Makefile adds -march=native -mtune=native on Linux and macOS arm64, so a binary built on one machine may not run on an older CPU; copy the release binary or build on the target class of host.

Benchmark harness note (ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark scripts/update.ts): each engine runs dist/run.js once, sequentially, on a shared GitHub runner, and the engines do not run it in the same mode (Node treats it as an ES module because the repo's package.json sets type: module, lo forces --use-strict, d8 runs it as a classic script); the effect on scores was not measured.

Most of the macOS and windows lead comes from Node's Splay score collapsing on those runners (15574 and 13056 vs 35204 on ubuntu, while lo and d8 stay near 35000-50000); excluding Splay, lo/Node is about 1.09x ubuntu, 1.26x macOS arm64 and 1.01x windows (derived from page data). The cause of Node's Splay drop is not documented.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick lo over LLRT when the work is compute-bound: in the same table LLRT scores 972 on ubuntu against lo's 43804, while LLRT's case is Lambda cold start; the other catalogued siblings speed up Python, Ruby, Lua or PHP, not JavaScript.
verified_claims_summary: Third-party daily CI table (ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark, fork of Mozilla arewefastyet v8-v7, snapshot 2026-10-05): lo 0.0.33.pre (V8 15.2) scored 43804 vs Node 26.10.0 (V8 14.6) 40333 on ubuntu-latest, 52785 vs 37405 on macos-latest arm64 and 40191 vs 35121 on windows-latest, one run each on GitHub-hosted runners with unstated CPUs and stripped prebuilt binaries; d8 15.7 beat lo on all three, and Bun canary and Deno canary scored below lo.
status_note: Active (ten pre-releases from 0.0.24-pre to 0.0.33-pre in August 2026, last commit 2026-09-16) and MIT-licensed, but still pre-1.0 with its own non-Node API, so treat it as an experimental runtime rather than a Node replacement.
